The week

Five days, about five hours a day, in the office with Harry and the team

Each day has a theme, a rough timetable and a question to reflect on. The timetable is a guide, not a contract. If something catches your interest, stay with it. Days run from about 10:00 to 15:30, with lunch in the middle.

Your open project

Through the week you can, if you like, follow one question of your own. There is no required format and no deadline. It could be a short note, a chart, a few slides, or just a conversation. If you want to share it on Friday, there is a slot for that. If you would rather not, that is completely fine. The point is to learn as much as you wish.

Some questions to start from, or to ignore:

  • How has mobile connectivity changed the economy of a country you know or would like to know?
  • Why is mobile data so much cheaper in some countries than in others?
  • Who still does not use mobile internet, and what would change that?

The mobile economy

Time Activity
10:00 Welcome, office tour and a coffee with Harry
10:45 Read the home page of this site; questions about GSMA and GSMA Intelligence
11:30 Guided tour of a public Mobile Economy report: how it is built, what each chart says
12:30 Lunch
13:00 Meet some of the team. Ask each person what a normal day looks like for them
14:00 Start your own glossary: ten terms from today you did not know (the Glossary can help)
14:45 Choose an open-project question, if you want one
15:15 Reflection and wrap-up

Reflect. What surprised you most about how big, or how small, the mobile industry is?

Growth and productivity

Time Activity
10:00 Read chapter 6 of Measuring the Economy on economic growth
11:00 Discussion with Harry: productivity, innovation and technology. Where does mobile fit?
11:45 Hands-on: download GDP per person and mobile subscriptions for three countries from the World Bank and chart them
12:30 Lunch
13:00 Read Paul Krugman’s “How I Work”
14:00 Open project time
15:15 Reflection and wrap-up

Reflect. Does a rise in mobile use cause growth, or does growth cause a rise in mobile use? How could you tell the difference?

Policy levers: spectrum, taxation and competition

Time Activity
10:00 Spectrum in plain English: what it is, why governments auction it, what can go wrong
11:00 Case study: a mobile tax. Who pays, who gains, and what happens to adoption?
12:00 Sit in on a team meeting
12:30 Lunch
13:00 Chat with a colleague who works on competition or regulation
14:00 Open project time
15:15 Reflection and wrap-up

Reflect. If you were a finance minister, would you tax mobile services more or less? What would you need to know first?

Development, inclusion and AI for economic research

Time Activity
10:00 The usage gap: who is not online and why. Skim the State of Mobile Internet Connectivity report
11:00 Agentic AI for economic research, with Harry. How Harry uses Claude at work: finding and checking sources, cleaning data, writing code, and why every result still needs a human check. Hands-on
12:30 Lunch
13:00 Agentic AI session continues: try it on your open-project question
14:00 Open project time
15:15 Reflection and wrap-up

Reflect. What can an AI assistant do well for an economist, and what should it never be trusted to do alone?

Sharing what we learn

Time Activity
10:00 Prepare for the afternoon: questions for the team, final touches to your open project if you have one
11:00 Harry’s presentation to GSMA Intelligence on how the team uses agentic AI in its research, including a telecoms news radar and a mobile tariffs tracker. You attend as part of the audience
12:00 Questions and lunch with the team
13:00 Optional: share your open project with Harry and the team, in any form
14:00 Looking ahead: economics at university, and what to read next (see Economic resources)
15:00 Feedback on the week and goodbye

Reflect. What is one thing an economist at GSMA Intelligence does that you did not expect on Monday?
